title: Euro area monetary developments — M3 and MFI loans (Sep 2026)
source: EST: ecb.europa.eu — CONFIRMED THIS SESSION ON TWO INDEPENDENT ECB PRIMARIES, both fetched direct 2026-09-05 by plain curl and parsed from their own text layers: the statistical calendars index (press/calendars/statscal, HTTP 200, 114,879 bytes) and this series' OWN DEDICATED RELEASE CALENDAR (press/calendars/statscal/mfm/html/stprmp, HTTP 200, 99,500 bytes) — a different page maintained for this dataset alone, whose five rows are Aug-2026 on 25/09/2026, Sep-2026 on 27/10/2026, Oct-2026 on 26/11/2026, Nov-2026 on 30/12/2026 and Dec-2026 on 29/01/2027. Both read verbatim "27/10/2026 10:00 CET", "Monetary developments in the euro area (Dataset: BSI)", "Reference period: Sep-2026", "Includes press release". Corroborated a third way on the realized record: all 113 releases from the Monetary Developments index (Mar-2017 -> Jul-2026, each publication date read off its own isoDate attribute and paired with its own md<YYMM> reference-month slug) put 9 OF 9 SEPTEMBER REFERENCE MONTHS IN THE 24-28 OCTOBER BAND (2017-10-26, 2018-10-24, 2019-10-28, 2020-10-27, 2021-10-27, 2022-10-26, 2023-10-25, 2024-10-25, 2025-10-27), with 107 of 113 on the 24th-30th of the following month overall; the six exceptions are November reference months pushed into early January by the Christmas period. No working-day formula fits (the 19th TARGET working day matches only 57 of 113), so the derivation is published calendar plus empirical band, not a rule. Stays estimate per the event-research lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep, and because CONFIRMED_PREFIX has no slot for a non-Fed central bank, checked 2026-09-05
notes: PROPOSED BECAUSE IT MAKES 2026-10-27 UNATTRIBUTABLE, not for a price channel — there is none and low is affirmed. This publishes at the SAME 10:00 CET MINUTE as ecb-bank-lending-survey-2026-10-27, as does the MFI national balance sheet (BSI, Sep-2026); three ECB releases share that slot, all inside the 10-21 -> 10-27 quiet period. So no euro move at 05:00 ET on 10-27 can be read off 'the bank lending survey' — the attribution is undecidable between three releases, which is the finding that demoted its sibling's reason for existing. WHY THIS ONE AND NOT THE OTHER SIX IN-WINDOW RELEASES: it is the only one carrying HARDER AND NEWER DATA THAN THE SURVEY IT COLLIDES WITH. The BLS is a qualitative net-percentage survey of banks about a quarter that closed four weeks earlier (the Oct-2025 round was conducted 19 Sep -> 7 Oct for a 10-28 release); this is the actual September count of M3 and of MFI loans to firms and households. It is also the series the ECB's own monetary policy statement quotes: the 2025-12-18 statement reads verbatim 'Bank lending to firms grew by 2.9 per cent on a yearly basis in October'. The other six were deliberately left unfiled — two are ECB-marked Tentative, four are government-finance statistics with no channel to this book, and filing them would spend six research sessions re-establishing a null already measured once. NO PRICE CHANNEL AND NONE CLAIMED: symbols: [], no house playbook is rates-keyed, and this book's exposure to euro policy is second-order via dollar translation and global term premium, both owned by the FOMC entries. CORRIDOR: 05:00 ET on FOMC Day 1, ahead of durable goods 08:30 ET and consumer confidence 10:00 ET the same morning, with the ECB's own decision 10-29. Discovered during the ecb-bank-lending-survey-2026-10-27 initial research (2026-09-05). AMENDED 2026-09-05 by this event's own initial research (docs/research/events/ecb-monetary-developments-2026-10-27.md); date, status, impact and symbols UNCHANGED, the date STRENGTHENED (see source), the collision finding INTACT, and the REASON FOR THE ENTRY UPGRADED while one phrase above is CORRECTED. (1) 'HARDER AND NEWER' IS HALF WRONG. Harder is right — this is a quantitative count (July 2026 press release, fetched: M3 +3.4% y/y, M1 3.1%, adjusted loans to households 3.1%, to non-financial corporations 4.4%) against the BLS's qualitative net percentages. NEWER IS NOT: the Oct-2025 BLS round was conducted 19 Sep -> 7 Oct, so the survey's field close is LATER than this print's 30 September reference-month end, and it carries a forward Q4-expectations component a backward monthly count does not. This series also REVISES its own headline numbers (the July release restates June M1 'revised from 3.4%'). Read it as HARDER AND MORE RECENTLY PUBLISHED. (2) THE BETTER REASON THE ENTRY EARNS: it is the last hard monetary input the Governing Council receives before it decides on 10-29. All five 2026 monetary policy statements were fetched direct (is260205, is260319, is260430, is260611, is260723) and 5 OF 5 QUOTE THIS SERIES BY NUMBER, always the MOST RECENTLY PUBLISHED MONTH — Dec-2025 on 02-05, Jan on 03-19, Mar on 04-30, Apr on 06-11, May on 07-23 — and the decisive precedent is 2026-04-30, which quoted March data published 2026-04-29, ONE DAY EARLIER. The 10-27 -> 10-29 gap is two days. Control on the same five: the bank lending survey is named in exactly the 3 statements that follow a round and in NEITHER of the two that do not. Registered as FT-ecb-monetary-developments-2026-10-27-1. (3) THE RELEASE DAY IS A FIRMER NULL THAN ITS SIBLING'S, ON THREE TIMES THE SAMPLE. Across the 44 releases since 2023-01-01, mean close-to-close |ret| vs an all-days baseline (Yahoo adjusted bars, instrument cache busted 2026-09-05): EXV1.DE euro bank equities 0.75% vs 0.95% (0.79x, against the BLS's 0.94x on n=14), Euro Stoxx 50 0.89x, DAX 0.88x, EUR/USD 0.96x, VIX 0.75x, S&P 500 0.70x; medians agree (0.78x/0.80x/0.92x) and a month-end control (day-of-month >= 22) still leaves 0.91x on the direct channel. 2x sessions: EXV1.DE 1 of 44 vs 10.5% of ordinary days. The 2017+ window (112 releases) lifts VIX to 1.15x and S&P to 1.19x ON MEANS ONLY — medians are 1.06x/1.01x and dropping the top three release sessions returns 0.96x/1.04x; those three are 2021-11-26 (Omicron), 2020-02-27 and 2020-03-26 (COVID), i.e. exogenous shocks that fell on a release date. (4) AND THE NULL SURVIVES A REAL SURPRISE AXIS, WHICH THE SIBLING'S COULD NOT BE TESTED AGAINST: unlike the BLS this series is polled. The best-documented instance is Jan-2026 M3 at 3.3% y/y vs 2.9% expected (Trading Economics, search-grade not primary), released 2026-02-26 — EXV1.DE +0.16%, Euro Stoxx 50 -0.19%, EUR/USD +0.34%, S&P 500 -0.54%. A +0.4pp beat produced a sixth of an ordinary day. (5) THE COLLISION IS RARER THAN IT READS: cross-checking the 113 release dates against the sibling's 14 BLS dates, the two series have collided ONCE SINCE 2023 (2023-05-02) — the BLS is anchored to Governing Council Day 1 and this release to the reference month, so 2026-10-27 is an unusual configuration with no historical template, which sharpens rather than weakens the attribution warning. (6) THE LIVE SUBSTANCE, and the only thing here worth watching: adjusted loans to non-financial corporations ran Dec 3.0 -> Jan 2.8 -> Feb 3.0 -> Mar 3.2 -> Apr 3.4 -> May 4.0 -> Jun 4.0 -> Jul 4.4% (+1.6pp over six non-declining months) with M3 at 3.4% in July — credit accelerating INTO a tightening cycle. Registered as FT-ecb-monetary-developments-2026-10-27-2. kind 'macro-print' fits better here than on its sibling (a scheduled numeric series WITH a published consensus and a surprise axis); impact stays low and symbols: [] is correct. The Aug-2026 print on 2026-09-25 was deliberately NOT filed as its own entry — same release one month earlier, measured null on n=44, and filing each monthly instance would spend twelve research sessions a year re-deriving one document.
